__comment: The Sky Dial (doc 23, 'The Sky Dial'): a Hearthblock window onto the sky over a plate with the time, the date and the year's seasons.
UIRegistry owns this file. WorldClock, SkyController and WeatherManager own the live state; the dial keeps none of its own.
The pieces are models in tools/hearthblock/art/sky.mjs, staged by tools/voxel_assets/build.py sky and rendered to layers in 'layers' by tools/GenerateUiIcons.gd.

picture: the framing every layer shares, in the window's cells seen from the front tilted down by 'pitch' degrees: [left, bottom, width, height] of the camera plane, where across is x and up is y * cos(pitch) - z * sin(pitch). 'width' is the layers' size in pixels across (twice the dial's width on screen).
opening: where moving pieces may show, in the same plane: the sun and moon, the drifting clouds and the falling rain or snow.
arc: the sun's path from sunrise on the left to sunset on the right, and the moon's through the night: its centre (x, y, z in cells) and radii.
clouds: where the clouds sit at midnight [x, y, z, 'big' or 'small']; they drift right by 'drift' cells a game hour and come round again.
fall: how fast rain and snow fall, in cells a game hour. They follow game time, so they stop when the game is paused.
weather: what each weather shows. 'grey' greys the daytime sky and hides the sun unless 'sun'; 'clouds' picks the cloud pieces (cloud or storm); 'fall' rain or snow; 'veil' mists the land.
seasons: the season bar's colour for each season, in the calendar's order.
